results.title: Nebius Watch: GPU Rent Price Hikes, a $2.6B Energy Deal, Nvidia Earnings, ClickHouse's $250 million ARR, and a New Whale in the Stock
highlights:
May 28, 2026

...

Today, I will break down the news that has accumulated over the past two weeks, specifically:

- Nebius’s GPU rental price hikes, effective June 1st.
- The strategic deal with Bloom Energy, totaling up to $2.6 billion.
- Nvidia’s quarterly earnings report.
- ClickHouse revealing a $250 million ARR.
- The news that the Situational Awareness fund, managed by Leopold Aschenbrenner, has become one of Nebius’s largest shareholders.

Let’s dive right in!

The GPU Rent Price Hikes

Starting June 1st, Nebius is increasing its on-demand (pay-as-you-go) rental rates. The price changes depend on the GPU model as follows:

- H100: From $2.95 to $3.85 (+30.5%)
- H200: From $3.50 to $4.50 (+28.6%)
- B200: From $5.50 to $7.15 (+30%)
- B300: From $6.10 to $7.85 (+28.7%)

Rates were also raised for interruptible capacity—meaning instances that are temporarily idle and haven’t been snatched up via standard on-demand agreements:

- H100: From $1.25 to $2.15 (+72%)
- H200: From $1.45 to $2.45 (+69%)
- B200: From $2.90 to $3.95 (+36%)
- B300: From $3.40 to $4.30 (+26.5%)

How does this pricing mechanism work? If Nebius has idle capacity—say, H100s—the company rents them out at a cheaper rate (at roughly a 45% discount to the on-demand price). However, if an on-demand customer shows up ready to pay the full rate, your workload gets interrupted and the capacity is reclaimed. This is an incredibly useful feature for startups with tight budgets and flexible computing timelines. For Nebius itself, it’s an excellent way to minimize downtime between major clients and boost overall GPU utilization.

Why does this matter?

The hike in on-demand pricing is the critical factor here, as long-term contracts are heavily influenced by it, and those rates will likely face upward revisions next. Broadly speaking, this move is yet another clear indicator that free capacity in the industry remains critically scarce. Yes, Nebius’s rates were initially lower than those offered by CoreWeave and the hyperscalers, so this gap can be gradually closed. But what really stands out is the price increase for Hopper—the previous-generation GPU. This directly reflects how deep the industry-wide shortage actually runs.

Obviously, once the acute shortage of compute resources eases across the market, prices for older models will slide. But right now, this gives Nebius a prime opportunity to squeeze maximum revenue out of the Hopper generation (where cards aren’t locked into long-term contracts) while securing higher top-line numbers from the Blackwell-generation GPUs being deployed now and over the coming quarters.

...

Of the remaining 70 MW, we don’t have exact data on the split between on-demand and long-term rentals. If we conservatively assume a 50/50 split, that leaves 35 MW for on-demand. Given the current average revenue of roughly $0.941 million per 1 MW per month, a 30% tariff hike on those “free” 35 MW will boost total average revenue to $0.999 million per 1 MW. This is the impact for the next quarter or two. Moving forward, I expect this pricing power to spill over into expiring contracts as they come up for renewal.

...

Non-hyperscaler clients (mostly neoclouds for now) brought in $37.4 billion (+31% QoQ and over 3x YoY). This is hardly surprising given how much neoclouds are expanding in both scale and absolute numbers.

...

In terms of the read-through for Nebius, there were positive data points: Huang mentioned that rental prices for older GPU generations have climbed since the start of the year—up 20% for the H100 (launched in 2022) and 15% for the A100 (launched in 2020). As I noted in the price hike section, this macro backdrop allows Nebius to squeeze maximum returns out of Hopper.

# [넥서스알파랩]신형 나왔는데 구형 값이 올랐다, 미국 AI 시장에서 벌어지는 진짜 권력 이동

## 엔비디아 칩 임대료 30퍼센트 폭등, 가격을 올린 건 엔비디아가 아니었다

2026.05.28| 조회 247 |

지난 한 달, 미국 인공지능 시장에서 상식을 뒤집는 일이 벌어졌습니다. 신형이 나왔는데 구형 가격이 같이 올랐습니다. 컴퓨터 부품 시장에서 이런 일은 거의 일어나지 않습니다. 신형이 나오면 구형은 자연스럽게 가격이 떨어집니다. 아이폰도 그렇고, 노트북도 그렇고, 자동차도 그렇습니다.

그런데 엔비디아의 인공지능 칩 시장에서는 정반대 일이 벌어졌습니다.

엔비디아 H100은 2년 전에 출시된 구형 모델입니다. 작년에 신형 B200이 시장에 나왔습니다. 그런데 지난 한 달 사이에 H100을 한 시간 빌리는 가격이 2달러 95센트에서 3달러 85센트로 올랐습니다. 약 30퍼센트 인상입니다. 신형 B200 임대료도 5달러 50센트에서 7달러 15센트로 함께 폭등했습니다.

구형도, 신형도, 모두 비싸졌습니다. 이것이 첫 번째 신호입니다.

여기서 진짜 충격적인 사실은 이 가격을 올린 회사가 엔비디아가 아니라는 점입니다. 엔비디아한테 칩을 잔뜩 사 와서 데이터센터에 꽂아두고, 다른 회사들에게 시간 단위로 빌려주는 새로운 임대업자들이 가격을 올렸습니다.

이 사업자들의 이름이 네오클라우드입니다. 코어위브, 네비우스, 화이트파이버 같은 회사들입니다. 사업 구조는 부동산 임대업과 거의 똑같습니다. 칩을 사 와서 자리에 꽂고, 시간당 임대료를 받습니다. 그런데 사업 총이익률이 약 65퍼센트에 달합니다. 일반 인프라 사업으로는 비정상적으로 높은 수익률입니다.

...

여기에 결정적인 사실 하나가 더해집니다.

...

이들은 자기들이 직접 데이터센터를 짓는 것보다 네오클라우드와 10년짜리 장기 계약을 맺는 것을 선택했습니다. 이유는 단순합니다. 직접 짓는 속도가 인공지능 수요를 도저히 못 따라가기 때문입니다.

results.title: GPU Rental Neoclouds vs AWS p5 p6 2026 | pdpspectra
highlights:
## The neocloud thesis in one paragraph#

Hyperscalers are vertically integrated. They sell you GPUs bundled with their networking, storage, IAM, observability, marketplace and a 30 to 50 percent gross-margin premium that funds the rest of the business. Neoclouds strip that down to the metal: NVIDIA reference designs, InfiniBand fabric, an object store, basic Kubernetes, and a sales team that returns your call the same day. The thesis is that for compute-bound training and high-throughput inference, the bundle is the cost, and unbundling delivers 30 to 60 percent savings. It works when your workload is GPU-dominated and self-contained. It breaks down when you need the rest of the cloud sitting next to it.

## The price curve for H100, H200, B100, B200#

Rough on-demand market pricing as of late May 2026 for a single GPU-hour, US regions:

| GPU | AWS p5/p6 list | CoreWeave on-demand | Lambda on-demand | RunPod Community | Together / Fireworks burst |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 80GB SXM | 4.10 to 4.90 | 2.20 to 2.79 | 2.49 to 2.99 | 1.79 to 2.49 | 2.10 to 2.79 |
| H200 141GB SXM | 5.49 to 6.30 | 2.99 to 3.79 | 3.29 to 3.99 | 2.79 to 3.49 | 3.10 to 3.79 |
| B100 (Blackwell) | 6.50 to 7.50 (limited) | 3.99 to 4.99 | 4.29 to 4.99 | 3.49 to 4.49 | not standard |
| B200 (Blackwell) | 8.50 to 9.50 (preview/limited) | 4.79 to 5.79 | 4.99 to 5.99 | 3.99 to 4.99 | 4.49 to 5.49 |

Three honest caveats on this table. First, AWS p5 and p6 list pricing is the on-demand sticker — almost nobody on serious volume pays it. EDP and reserved discounts pull effective rates down 30 to 55 percent. Second, neocloud headline rates almost always assume a multi-month reservation or a credit-card on-demand pool that runs out of supply quickly. Third, B100 and B200 supply through every channel was still rationed through Q1 2026, so quoted rates are softer than they look.

The honest takeaway: for a one-year H100 commit, the neocloud rate is in the 1.60 to 2.10 range; the hyperscaler reserved rate is in the 2.40 to 3.20 range. That gap funds the neocloud thesis.

...

## The Blackwell transition#

B100 and B200 supply through 2025 was rationed first to hyperscalers and the largest labs. Neoclouds got meaningful B200 capacity starting late Q4 2025 and through Q1 2026. By mid-2026 the curve is normal: any serious neocloud customer can reserve B200s on a 3-to-6 month lead time. The practical question for most teams is whether B200’s roughly 2 to 3x throughput on the right workloads is worth the 1.6 to 1.9x price multiple — and whether their software stack actually exploits it. vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, and SGLang have all had production Blackwell support for a while; PyTorch is mature; many in-house training stacks still need real tuning work to see the full uplift.

results.title: Six months ago people had barely heard of the Pro 6000 Blackwell... Today teams are paying nearly 2x to get on it. | Jack Skywalker
highlights:
Six months ago people had barely heard of the Pro 6000 Blackwell... Today teams are paying nearly 2x to get on it.

Here's what changed:

H100 capacity is scarce. B200 capacity is scarcer. Often locked behind multi-year contracts.

If you want FP4 or FP8 quantized inference without multi-node scaling, the Pro 6000 is one of the only viable options left.

96GB GDDR7. Native FP4 via Blackwell architecture. A 70B class model fits cleanly at FP8 on a single node... no multi-node networking required. You can also split one GPU into three or four parallel MIG instances for mixed workload serving.

Six months ago the tooling wasn't mature. Teams couldn't get the cost-performance to work.

That's no longer true.

Now it's the default answer for inference serving that don't need multi-node scale... and everyone figured that out at the same time.

Pricing moved from ~$0.85 to $1.45/hr and it's still climbing.

NVIDIA is raising hardware prices across the board by 30%. New capacity will no longer carry the current sticker price. Existing inventory is getting scooped up fast.

If you're looking at Pro 6000 capacity today, time is running out to lock in at current rates.

The teams that secured at $1.05 have a real cost advantage right now.

The teams still shopping? They're inheriting the new pricing tier.

results.title: The NVIDIA H100 in 2026: A 12× Price Spread for the Same Silicon | emma Blog
highlights:
## TL;DR

- H100 cloud rentals span $1.38/hr to $12.29/hr in May 2026 — a 12× spread for identical silicon, depending entirely on where you buy it.
- Prices have dropped up to 70% from 2023 peaks when on-demand rates hit $8–11/hr. AWS and other hyperscalers reduced H100 pricing through 2025 as supply improved, contributing to broader market-wide cost compression.
- Specialized providers undercut hyperscalers by 3–5×, with spot or marketplace rates dropping near ~$1.5/hr, compared to ~$7–$12/hr on hyperscaler platforms
- Cost-per-token, not hourly rate, is what actually matters. At low batch sizes a "cheap" H100 can cost 20× more per million tokens than a properly configured one.
- The H100 is now the cost-performance sweet spot, not the frontier. B200 and B300 (Blackwell) are shipping, but the H100 remains

...

## What actually changed between 2023 and 2026

Three forces collapsed H100 pricing. First, supply caught up: TSMC expanded CoWoS packaging capacity through 2024, and refurbished cards started flowing into secondary markets. 

Second, competition arrived from below — Vast.ai, RunPod, Hyperbolic, Runcrate, and dozens of specialized GPU clouds built lean, GPU-only businesses that hyperscalers could not match on raw price. 

Third, the next generation arrived. With B200 (Blackwell) shipping from late-2025 and B300 from January 2026, the H100 is no longer the frontier chip, and frontier-chip pricing power has migrated up the stack.

AWS's June 2025 decision to cut P5 prices by 44% was the catalytic moment. Within weeks, the entire industry repriced. Today's pricing landscape looks nothing like the launch market.

...

The honest summary: If you want the cheapest H100, you can find one on a specialized provider for $1.49–$2.10/hr. If you want enterprise SLAs and integrated tooling, expect to pay $3.50–$7/hr on hyperscalers.

results.title: B200 Rental Market Splits into Wholesale and Hyperscaler Pricing | GPUaaS.com posted on the topic | LinkedIn
highlights:
# B200 Rental Market Splits into Wholesale and Hyperscaler Pricing

The B200 rental market has quietly split in two. Same chip. Same generation. Same NVIDIA Blackwell silicon. Different prices depending on where you buy it. Current B200 cloud rental spread, as of May 2026: → Wholesale floor: ~$2.99/GPU/hr → On-demand mid-market: ~$6/GPU/hr → Hyperscaler on-demand: ~$10-12/GPU/hr That's roughly a 3-4x spread on the same hardware, before enterprise contract premiums. A few things driving this: → Supply is still constrained. Demand exceeds supply by an estimated 1.4-1.6x, and the bottleneck is TSMC's CoWoS packaging, not the chips themselves. → Agentic inference workloads have changed the demand profile. Token generation volumes went exponential as multi-step agentic workflows moved into production, which keeps utilization high and spot availability low. → Hyperscaler pricing bakes in compliance, enterprise contracts, and SLA bundles. Wholesale pricing doesn't. The takeaway most buyers miss: the headline B200 rate on a hyperscaler quote isn't the market price. It's near the top of a band that runs 3-4x deep. Worth knowing where on that band you're sitting before signing. DM us or click the link in the first comment. #AIInfrastructure #GPUCloud #B200 #BlackwellGPU #AICompute
